title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Iran has offered a two-week regional truce in return for a gradual reopening of Hormuz, but the Tehran talks ended with no breakthrough and Iran says another tanker hit a mine. Brent fell to $113.88, while Saudi air suspensions were pushed further out, so road into KSA stays our main lane into November.

stories.headline: Iran offers a two-week truce and a gradual Hormuz reopening, but no deal yet
body: At the Tehran talks on 26 October, Iran offered a two-week pause in hostilities across the region. In return, the Strait of Hormuz would gradually reopen. Iran asked Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey to persuade Washington to accept it.

Sources told The National there was no clear breakthrough; the main result was an agreement to keep talking, possibly in Turkey. Hours later, Saudi forces intercepted more Houthi missiles and drones, including two aimed at Riyadh.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: a concrete reopening offer, but tied to US approval. Keep Gulf inbound sea on war terms and do not plan on a reopening this side of the 3 November US midterms.

stories.headline: Iran says a tanker hit a mine east of Hormuz, two days after the US said the lanes were clear
body: Iran's army said on 27 October that an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted area east of the strait, with its tracking switched off. On 25 October the US military had said the main lanes were free of Iranian mines.

Iran says tankers must coordinate passage with it in advance. It also claims mine strikes on two VLCCs on 23 October and three tankers on 20 October. None of these claims has been independently confirmed.
stories.soWhat: Mine claims keep war-risk insurance high. Keep sea surcharges indexed and steer urgent cargo to Khor Fakkan, Fujairah or Sohar.

stories.headline: Saudi flight suspensions pushed into late November
body: Lufthansa Group has suspended Riyadh until 18 November and Dammam through 30 November. Akasa stays off Riyadh to 30 November, Air India to 7 November and Etihad to 5 November. flydubai's Riyadh, Dammam and Abha suspension runs to 29 October, and Emirates and Air Arabia gave no restart date.
British Airways plans a limited daily Riyadh service from 3 November. On 27 October Saudi air defences intercepted two more Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh.
stories.soWhat: New: several carriers now stay out until mid or late November. Belly space into KSA stays scarce, so keep road as the default and offer KSA road rates through November.

stories.headline: UAE departing seats up 23% since June
body: Departing seats at UAE airports rose 23% to 7.2 million between June and October, with Dubai leading. Up to 36 weekly Dubai–Europe flights are due back by December.
stories.soWhat: More belly capacity out of the UAE. A good moment to re-tender outbound air buy rates before peak.

stories.headline: E-invoicing: firms above Dh50 million must appoint a provider by 30 October
body: UAE businesses with annual revenue of Dh50 million or more must appoint an accredited e-invoicing provider by 30 October and go live by 1 January 2027. Smaller firms have until 31 March 2027 to appoint and 1 July 2027 to go live.
The Federal Tax Authority fine is Dh5,000 for each month or part month of delay, and it applies to missing the appointment deadline too.
stories.soWhat: Our large B2B accounts will change how they receive and match invoices from January. Billing should confirm we are ready and tell key accounts.

stories.headline: Al Sharqi opens a Dh70 million cold-chain hub in Dubai Industrial City
body: Al Sharqi Shipping has opened a hub with 280,000 sq ft of storage and 22,000 palletised tonnes of multi-temperature space, from ambient to -18°C. It has 38 loading lanes for up to 178 trucks a day.
It targets food, FMCG, retail, hotels and quick commerce, and sits near Jebel Ali, Al Maktoum airport and an Etihad Rail freight terminal.
stories.soWhat: New cold-chain capacity aimed at food and q-commerce clients we also chase. Expect sharper pricing on Dubai food and FMCG contract logistics bids.

competitors.name: UPS
competitors.headline: Q3 revenue up 6.7% to $22.9bn; international revenue per piece up 15%
body: UPS reported on 27 October. International revenue rose 7.1% to $5.0 billion, driven by a 15.0% rise in revenue per piece, with a 14.9% operating margin. It raised guidance: Q4 revenue of about $25.7 billion and full-year revenue of about $92.6 billion.
The release made no specific comment on Middle East surcharges or fuel.
competitors.soWhat: Integrators are pushing yield, not volume, on international. There is room to hold our international express rates and surcharges through peak.

competitors.name: noon
competitors.headline: noon Send for Business powers a 30-minute q-commerce service for UAE brands
body: Dubai fulfilment platform Shorages launched Q-Com, which delivers eligible orders within 30 minutes of being packed. noon Send for Business handles the last mile. It starts with existing Shorages customers in the UAE.
competitors.soWhat: noon is selling its last mile to third-party brands through fulfilment partners. Our e-commerce team should pitch same-day and fulfilment bundles to the same D2C brands.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo / Emirates Courier Express
competitors.headline: Freighter fleet growing to 23 by March 2027 as Courier Express signs Dubai brands
body: Emirates SkyCargo has taken seven Boeing 777 freighters since March 2026 plus its first converted 777-300ERSF, and expects 23 dedicated freighters by end-March 2027. Freighter destinations grew from just over 40 to over 60 between March and July.
Its Emirates Courier Express door-to-door service now names Dubai brands Squatwolf, Mayple Global and Magrabi Optical as users for GCC and global shipping (Asia Cargo News, 15 Oct).
competitors.soWhat: Emirates is going after the same Dubai D2C exporters as our international express. Protect key e-commerce accounts with transit-time and rate reviews before renewals.

competitors.name: J&T Express
competitors.headline: Q3 volume outside Asia up 159.5%; Middle East named as a growth market
body: J&T moved 9.58 billion parcels in Q3, up 24.8%. Its 'Other Markets' segment, which includes the Middle East, rose 159.5% to 270.8 million parcels. No UAE or Saudi split was given.
competitors.soWhat: J&T is scaling fast in new markets and competes on price. Watch our low-value e-commerce lanes in KSA and UAE for undercutting.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Latest result: record Q2 revenue of Dh1.83 billion
body: Revenue rose 22% to Dh1.83 billion in Q2 2026, the highest in our history. Net profit was Dh47 million, about seven times a year earlier, and the EBITDA margin rose to 9.9% from 7%. Q3 results are not yet out.
competitors.soWhat: Freight and domestic carried the quarter. Protect those margins as KSA air stays shut and new cold-chain and q-commerce rivals price in.

opportunities.title: KSA road through late November
opportunities.text: Lufthansa, Akasa and Air India now stay out of Saudi airports into November. Road express and FTL into KSA should stay in demand.

opportunities.title: Cheaper outbound air buy
opportunities.text: UAE departing seats are up 23% since June and more Europe flights return by December. Re-tender our air buy rates.

opportunities.title: E-invoicing ready billing
opportunities.text: Large customers must go live with e-invoicing on 1 January. Clean, compliant invoices can be a selling point for key accounts.

opportunities.title: Same-day for D2C brands
opportunities.text: noon and Emirates are both courting Dubai D2C brands. A fulfilment plus same-day bundle can win them first.

opportunities.title: Price discipline on international
opportunities.text: UPS grew international revenue per piece by 15%. The market supports holding our yields through peak.

watchouts.title: Hormuz deal tied to Washington
watchouts.text: Iran's reopening offer needs US approval, and Trump has floated action after the 3 November midterms. Escalation is still possible.

watchouts.title: Mine claims east of Hormuz
watchouts.text: Iran says another tanker hit a mine. War-risk cover and sea surcharges will stay high.

watchouts.title: Houthi fire on Riyadh
watchouts.text: More missiles were intercepted over Riyadh on 27 October. KSA restart dates could slip again.

watchouts.title: E-invoicing penalties
watchouts.text: Dh5,000 a month for late appointment. Check our own status and our system's fit with customers' providers.

watchouts.title: New cold-chain rivals
watchouts.text: Al Sharqi's Dh70 million Dubai hub adds food and q-commerce capacity that will compete on price.

watchouts.title: Fuel prices for November
watchouts.text: UAE announces November fuel prices around 31 October. Brent is still near $114.

moves.title: Offer KSA road rates to 30 November
moves.text: Saudi air suspensions now run into mid and late November. Lock in road volume before customers look elsewhere.

moves.title: Re-tender outbound air buy rates
moves.text: Use the 23% rise in UAE seats and returning Europe flights to ask carriers for lower rates before peak.

moves.title: Confirm our e-invoicing readiness this week
moves.text: Check our provider status before 30 October and send key accounts a short note on how invoices will reach them from January.

moves.title: Hold international express yields through peak
moves.text: UPS is growing revenue per piece by 15%. Avoid discounting international express to win volume.

moves.title: Pitch a D2C fulfilment and same-day bundle
moves.text: Target Dubai brands courted by noon Send and Emirates Courier Express with one price for storage, pick-pack and same-day.

moves.title: Sharpen food and FMCG cold-chain bids
moves.text: Expect Al Sharqi to price aggressively from its new hub. Review our cold-chain rate cards for Dubai food clients.

moves.title: Prepare a November diesel surcharge update
moves.text: Be ready to move road surcharges the day UAE fuel prices come out, around 31 October.
